assertion_analysis.assertions: removed equals an independently empty list for six unusable result variants
assertion_analysis.fails_if: Reinstating the prior role-only exemption deletes r-reviewer and yields a nonempty removal list; the recorded reversal demonstrates all six failures.
Removing the reviewer despite a withheld report makes is_dir false; restoring the prior guard-free behavior also deletes it.
Restoring the old review-of-self guard returns review-owed rather than the result-specific category; bypassing both guards leaves no withheld row.
Returning the prior review-owed reason or a generic reason without the reviewer-result explanation makes substring membership false.

assertion_analysis.assertions: removed identifies the planted old reviewer for staging and plan locations
assertion_analysis.fails_if: Removing staging lookup or restricting committed lookup to run subjects retains the reviewer and returns an empty removal list; directory.name is independently observed filesystem identity rather than a returned-value echo.
Reporting prune without performing removal leaves the directory present.

assertion_analysis.assertions: stored review outside the retired directory survives
assertion_analysis.fails_if: Expanding deletion to the surviving staging or plan result removes target and makes is_file false.

findings.text: blocking: The committed index is keyed by path.stem and queried with the bare reviewer run ID at line 366, while review.py:2732-2743 files figure reviews as figure.<review-run-id>.at-<head>.json; when the staging record is absent, a valid committed figure review is therefore reported as missing-review-result and its old reviewer directory can never retire, so resolve reviewer identity using the store owner and cover this committed-only case.
